We establish a kinematic model of Wheeled Mobile Robots (WMR) and design a new Lyapunov equation to extend the attractive domain of steering angle error. Cross terms are introduced to eliminate the need for separate consideration of the traditional Lyapunov equation. Unknown slip is represented as an unknown parameter in the kinematic model and estimated using an adaptive law. The asymptotic stability of the tracking error system is proved. Our proposed control law demonstrates improved stability and effectiveness compared to two reference trajectories, as confirmed by simulations.

articleTitle: Binocular Depth Estimation Method for Stereo Matching Based on Pyramid Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Stereoscopic matching technology holds significant importance in fields such as virtual reality, 3D reconstruction, and autonomous driving. The key to achieving this technology lies in accurate depth estimation. Our aim is to address the challenge of CNNs struggling to learn global and long-range contextual information during feature extraction in stereo matching and to enhance the accuracy of depth estimation. To achieve this goal, we propose SPTNet (Stereo Pyramid Transformer Net), a binocular stereo matching method. We utilize STTR (STereo Transformer) as the backbone network and replace traditional CNN -based feature extraction with Transformer-based methods. Additionally, we introduce a multi-scale feature fusion module to ensure that the output features contain both shallow and deep semantic information. While performing epipolar rectification, we use correlation operations to compute the cost volume. During training, we incorporate a feature differentiation loss function to enhance the model's attention to details and, consequently, improve the accuracy of the depth map. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on publicly available Sceneflow and KITTI datasets.

articleTitle: EASATrack: Infrared Object Tracking Based on Edge Activation and Scale Adaptive Cross-Correlation
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The blurring of object edges in infrared images and scale variations among consecutive frames largely affect the precision of existing tracking model. To this end, a model called EASATrack based on edge activation and scale adaptive cross-correlation is designed. First, in this model, an edge activation module is employed to amplify the edge information of the object within infrared images. Then, a scale adaptive cross-correlation module is designed to perceive object information across varying scales, thereby accommodating changes in object scale during similarity computations. Finally, to validate the proposed model, plenty experiments are conducted on publicly available datasets PTB-TIP and LSOTB-TIR. The results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves leading performance in terms of precision and success rate on both datasets.

articleTitle: A Study of Puncture Target Following Based on K-Nearest Neighbor Regression Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In the process of using a robot to puncture lung nodules or tumors, respiratory motion can cause the target point to drift, affecting the accuracy of the puncture, so this paper proposes the use of the K nearest neighbor algorithm to predict the respiratory motion and then control the robotic arm to follow the movement of the puncture target point. After the hand-eye calibration of the robotic arm and the optical navigator, the robotic arm is controlled to move to the puncture target positioning tool, and with the patient's respiratory movement, the K nearest neighbor algorithm is used to predict the subsequent movement and control the robotic arm to move to the predicted position in real time, and finally the prediction results, the measurement results and the actual robotic arm movement results are compared to validate the accuracy and the real-time performance of the robotic arm to follow the target point movement.

articleTitle: Research on Adaptive Forward-Looking Distance Unmanned Vehicle Path Tracking Algorithm Based on Road Curvature
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In order to improve the path tracking accuracy and stability of low-speed autonomous vehicles during turning maneuvers, this study proposes an adaptive forward-looking distance path tracking algorithm based on road curvature. The algorithm utilizes vehicle localization data and the curvature information of the path at the look_ahead point. By combining a formula for adaptive forward-looking distance derived from extensive physical experiments, the algorithm adjusts the forward-looking distance to obtain appropriate look_ahead points and the steering angle of the autonomous vehicle's front wheels. While maintaining algorithm stability, it effectively reduces the lateral error of the autonomous vehicle during turning maneuvers. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed adaptive forward-looking distance path tracking algorithm outperforms traditional pure tracking algorithms in terms of accuracy and stability.

articleTitle: YOLO-FE: A Lightweight Ship Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In order to solve the deployment difficulties caused by low detection accuracy, large number of common model parameters and slow calculation speed of deep learning target detection models deployed on offshore unmanned platforms such as buoys. Based on the YOLOv8n model, this paper proposes an improved lightweight ship detection model YOLO-FE. Firstly, the BottleBlock of C2f module is replaced by FasterN et Block in the FasterNet module to reduce the complexity of the model and improve the calculation speed of the model. Secondly, the EMA attention mechanism is introduced to further save the computational cost, and the global context information can be better obtained by using the EMA attention mechanism. Finally, the experimental results show that on the self-made ship data set, compared with the original model YOLOv8 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>, YOLO-FE has the P, mAP0.5-0.95 increased by 2.1%and 0.2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>respectively, and the model parameters and GFLOPs reduced by 25.8%and 19.7%respectively. Compared with the common lightweight version of YOLO model, the YOLO-FE model is more lightweight and requires less computing resources while maintaining high accuracy for ship identification.

articleTitle: A Lightweight-Model Based Federated Learning Approach for Fault Diagnosis in Intelligent Power Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The federated learning framework plays a pivotal role in diagnosing faults in distribution equipment. Alleviating the computational complexity and communication burden of its micro-terminals is essential for enhancing the efficiency of the federated learning framework. Therefore, this paper focuses on effectively lightening the fault diagnosis model by employing a combination of model pruning and quantization techniques, aiming to compress the fault diagnosis model. To achieve this, we employ a two-step approach. Firstly, neural networks are pruned selectively based on the significance of the model's structure and weights, resulting in model compression. Secondly, a significant portion of the model parameters is mapped to a smaller set of representative vectors, leading to data compression, reduced storage requirements, and lowered data transmission costs. Compared with traditional methods, this approach reduces the computational load of the fault diagnosis model from 901.38M to 442.43M, with only a minor 2.5% decrease in diagnostic accuracy. This methodology not only ensures the security of the data but also adeptly addresses the constraints faced by micro-terminal devices in computing and communication within the distributed federated learning environment.

articleTitle: Rethinking the Helmet Wearing Detection Algorithm Based on Reinforcement Feature and Loss Function in Complex Tunnel Scenes
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Helmet wear detection is critical to protecting workers' lives in industrial settings. However, tunnel scenarios present challenges, such as small target sizes, significant scale variations, and occlusion issues, rendering traditional safety helmet detection methods less effective. To address the above problems, this paper proposes an end-to-end Enhanced Feature Detection Network (EFDNet). The innovations of EFDNet mainly include two points: Firstly, this paper proposes an Enhanced Feature Module (EFM), which enhances the texture shape of the target by amplifying the semantic information in the deep feature map and improves the focus on the tiny targets. Secondly, considering the difficulty of target regression with large-scale changes and the slow convergence speed of the model, this paper proposes a novel regression loss function called DTIoU. This loss function only considers the distance and spatial domain of the predicted and real box centroids to calculate the loss function value. Finally, this paper verifies the accuracy and robustness of EFDNet on the Hard Hat Workers dataset.

articleTitle: Research on Automatic Parking System for Four-wheeled Logistics Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This paper introduces a four-wheeled logistics robot automatic parking system based on hierarchical finite state machine. Aiming at the complexity of the open road parking scene of small logistics robots and the difficulty of guaranteeing the stability of automatic parking, the parking scene, system architecture design, and decision model design are studied. The design of robot control three-layer architecture, the use of hierarchical finite state machine technology, to achieve the design of high stability and high execution efficiency of the automatic parking system. By comparing the layered finite state machine model and the finite state machine model in five scenes, combined with the simulation of the model's scene adaptability, it is concluded that the automatic parking system based on layered finite state machine has good scene adaptability and stability.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Network-Based Linear Quadratic Programming for Vehicle Path Tracking
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Path tracking is a crucial component for achieving autonomous steering in self-driving vehicles. This paper presents a novel path tracking algorithm that utilizes a deep neural network (DNN) to learn steering actions, enabling autonomous path tracking for vehicles. The algorithm trains the deep neural network using input and output data derived from traditional control strategies. These traditional controllers encompass full-state feedback control designed through linear quadratic programming (LQR) and feedforward control that takes road curvature into account. State variables from the path tracking system, road curvature, and lateral vehicle speed serve as training inputs for the deep neural network, allowing the trained model to replicate the steering behavior of the traditional controller. Simulation results demonstrate that the trained model successfully accomplishes the tracking task and exhibits steering behavior equivalent to the LQR control method with feedforward control.

articleTitle: Optimizing Cooperative Control Algorithms for Vehicles and Roads at Unsignalized Intersections Considering Communication Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In the future, the need for traffic lights at intersections will be eliminated, and autonomous vehicles can be efficiently and safely controlled through an Intersection Control Center (ICC). This paper presents a novel unsignalized intersection control algorithm based on mixed integer nonlinear programming (MINP). By formulating the vehicle space-time trajectory conflict as a mathematical model, the algorithm takes into account various factors, including vehicle delay, fuel consumption, and dynamics constraints. The MINP problem is solved using a genetic algorithm to obtain the optimal vehicle trajectory. Moreover, recognizing the significance of network communication in intersection scheduling, the control algorithm also considers the influence of C-V2X communication performance. To validate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, a comprehensive joint simulation is conducted using SUMO and MATLAB, which replicates real urban intersections. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms traditional signal light control in terms of vehicle delay and fuel consumption.

articleTitle: An Estimation Strategy for Sideslip Angle Fusion Utilizing a Linear Adaptive Model
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This paper introduces a robust method for estimating the sideslip angle. We propose a fusion approach that integrates an adaptive linear model and a kinematic model to enhance the accuracy of sideslip angle estimation. The adaptive linear model is constructed based on a two-degree-of-freedom vehicle dynamics model, accounting for variations in speed and wheel parameters. Dynamic estimation of the sideslip angle is achieved through the utilization of the extended Kalman filter (EKF). To determine the sideslip angle, we employ the integral method, considering the relationship between the vehicle's lateral and longitudinal acceleration and the sideslip angle. Aiming at the disadvantage that the adaptive linear model estimation method can estimate the sideslip angle accurately only when there is lateral acceleration motion, a fusion transformation mechanism of the minimum mean square error weighted average method is designed to estimate the sideslip angle. The efficacy of the proposed approach is demonstrated through Simulink-Carsim joint simulation. The results reveal that employing both algorithms for sideslip angle estimation achieves greater accuracy compared to relying on a single estimation algorithm.

articleTitle: Concrete Crack Segmentation Using UNet Algorithm with Swin Transformer Block & CPAM
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Thereis a wide variety and large quantity of cracks on the surface of concrete, and different types of cracks have varying degrees of impact on structural safety. Some cracks may lead to significant safety incidents in the structure. Therefore, surface cracks in concrete are one of the important monitoring targets for structural health. This paper proposes a new neural network model - integrating Swin Transformer Block & CPAM into the Unet network, for intelligent recognition of concrete cracks. During the down-sampling process, the Swin Transformer Block is introduced. Following up-sampling in the Unet network, feature maps are extracted using this module as a separate branch, reshaped, and merged with the feature maps. The feature maps enter the dual attention module (CPAM) following the concatenation procedure. Eventually, Unet's down-sampled feature maps and the CPAM-processed feature maps are combined. By introducing the Unet network with Swin Transformer Block & CPAM, important information in the feature maps can be extracted and enhanced, thereby improving the model's ability to recognize target features. Through experiments, the Unet model with Swin Transformer Block & CPAM proposed in this paper is superior in results to UNet and Swin-UNet in recognizing concrete cracks. This approach effectively enhances the performance of semantic segmentation of concrete cracks and plays a positive role in enhancing the model's feature extraction and attention mechanism. This has significant implications for ensuring the safety and reliability of concrete structures.

articleTitle: Multimodal Fake News Detection Technology Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With the development of science and technology, incidents of fake news triggering social crises occur from time to time. The change of media media makes false news gradually change from text form to multi-modal form with graphic and text coexisting. Multimodal fake news carries heterogeneous forms of text and image information, and research on the multimodal content of fake news can improve the effect of fake news detection. Existing multimodal fake news detection methods have the following deficiencies. First of all, in terms of feature extraction, most methods do not consider their own effective features, and features are not universal at this stage. Secondly, in terms of feature fusion, in the previous fake news detection methods that used image features combined with text features, the feature information in the news was simply spliced, without considering the interactive information between the two modalities. Finally, in terms of model structure, few models can verify the effectiveness of extracted features. According to the problems encountered in the current research, this paper conducts multi-modal fake news detection research based on deep learning, which further improves the accuracy of false news detection.

articleTitle: Study Method of Blood Mechanical Damage Based on a Taylor-Couette Device
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Due to changes in modern living habits, cardiovascular disease has risen to become one of the leading causes of death worldwide. In response, the use of artificial hearts has emerged as an effective method for treating heart failure. Investigating the patterns of mechanical injury to blood is crucial in advancing artificial heart technology. Therefore, this article presents the development of a Taylor-Couette shear device capable of precisely controlling shear stress and exposure time. This design offers improved accuracy compared to previous iterations of the Taylor-Couette device. Additionally, the article proposes a research methodology for studying blood injury based on the characteristics of the device and the cells involved. The effectiveness of this research method is further explained from a biological perspective.

articleTitle: Multi-Ground-Robot System 3D Map Merging Method Based on Global Localization and Robust ICP
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Compared to a single robotic entity, Multi-Ground-Robot Systems (MGRS) prove to be more resilient and efficient in various applications, including unknown environment reconnaissance and rescue missions. In this paper, we introduce a novel 3D map merging method specifically tailored for MGRS. Initially, we employ a global localization procedure to determine an initial relative position guess for the robots. Subsequently, we leverage a robust and fast Iterative Closest Point (ICP) algorithm to identify a refined rigid transformation between local maps, thus merging the local maps accordingly. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of our approach using both open and self-collected datasets. The experiments reveal that our approach attains a fitness score of 0.07m and 0.09m across the two respective datasets. Additionally, when compared to the other merging techniques, our method yields superior fitness scores, owing to its enhanced resilience in noisy condition.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Urban Intersection C-V2X Simulation System
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In this study, we integrate C-V2X (Cellular Vehicle-to-Everything) technology with urban intersection scenarios and design and implement a comprehensive C-V2X system-level simulation platform. The platform encompasses three main modules: traffic simulation, network simulation, and performance evaluation. Using this simulation platform, we validate the reliability of the C-V2X system by assessing the array packet reception rate. The results demonstrate the high reliability of our system platform. Moreover, we evaluate the performance of LTE-V2X direct link broadcast communication under low, medium, and high vehicle density scenarios. Our findings indicate that the system's transmission performance deteriorates in high-density vehicle scenarios. Additionally, we assess the performance of NR-V2X direct link broadcast communication by examining the impact of the physical layer parameter SCS. The results reveal that increasing the SCS improves the transmission performance. Furthermore, we find that NR-V2X can enhance system performance through the flexible configuration of parameters. Our research contributes to the understanding of C-V2X technology in urban intersection environments and provides valuable insights for optimizing system performance and reliability.

articleTitle: An Improved A* Path Planning Algorithm for ROS Based Robots
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In the ROS environment, an improved A* algorithm is proposed to address a series of problems caused by the A* algorithm, such as too many turning points, paths close to obstacles, and often falling into a “false-death” state, for a mobile robot in a complex situation. Firstly, according to the radius of the chassis of the mobile robot, the radius of the obstacle expansion layer in the ROS grid cost map is increased, secondly, the heuristic function is modified to introduce the generation value of the cost map, so as to prioritize the passage of the region with a lower generation value in the planning of global paths, and finally, the paths are further simplified by the method of straightening and de-pointing for the global paths so as to be easier for the control of the robot. Simulation results show that the improved A* algorithm can effectively keep the planned path away from obstacles, reduce the chance of collision of the robot, reduce the frequency of “false death” state of the robot, and improve the stability of the robot.

articleTitle: Resilient Control Strategy for Seaport Microgrid Against False Data Injection Attacks Based on Interactive System
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: One of the most popular control strategies for seaport microgrids (SMGs) is distributed control because it efficiently combines the benefits of centralized control with distributed control, lowers communication and calculation complexity, and enhances dependability and scalability of the system. The stability of the system and the safety of the inverter are at risk, though, because there is no central controller for monitoring the activities of the generator set. As a result, under the influence of potential network attacks, the control decisions between distributed generations (DGs) will be directly destroyed, and the power sharing between DGs will be hampered. To address the secondary control problem of the microgrid under false data injection (FDI) attacks, inspired by the concept of Digital Twins, this study proposes a virtual network defined by cloud network technology or software and linked to the microgrid's distributed cooperative control algorithm, to achieve frequency (voltage) synchronization and power sharing of SMGs.

articleTitle: End-to-End Autonomous Driving Decision-Making Solution Based on Pri-TD3
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In order to address the issue of information loss in traditional hierarchical autonomous driving systems and enhance the decision-making capabilities of autonomous vehicles in complex environments, a deep reinforcement learning-based end-to-end autonomous driving solution is proposed. The Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithm is capable of achieving superior policies for continuous action control compared to algorithms such as Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) and Deep Q-Network (DQN). However, it suffers from the problem of low sample efficiency. To address this issue, this paper introduces an improved Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (Pri-TD3) algorithm based on the prioritized experience replay technique. Additionally, the algorithm is validated through simulations in a scenario involving multiple vehicles making unprotected left turns using the Carla simulator. Results demonstrate that the proposed Pri-TD3 algorithm outperforms DDPG and TD3 in terms of convergence speed, reward acquisition, and policy stability, etc.

articleTitle: A novel Multi-Label Leaming Approach for Missing and Noisy Labels
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Recently, many scholars have shown a strong interest in weak-supervised multi-label learning, to solving which idealizing label information is a common approach. However, in real life, we cannot obtain the complete labels of instances. In addition, the obtained labels may contain noise, which can reduce the performance of the algorithms. To address the above issues, we introduce MLML, a novel multi-label learning method which is designed specifically to handle missing labels and noisy labels simultaneously. Our method involves the following several steps. Firstly, we utilize the global information of multi-label data to construct a label correlation matrix. Through this matrix, we can better understand the association and influence between different labels. Secondly, in order to mitigate the impact of noisy labels, we introduce label popularity normalization, which improves the performance of the algorithm by considering the frequency of labels in the data. Finally, we improve the method by integrating positive and negative label information. We also consider the relationship between feature similarity and label similarity, which ensures that our method not only considers the information of a single label, but also the mutual influence between labels and the association between features and labels. Based on extensive experiments conducted on multiple datasets, our algorithm MLML has demonstrated comparable performance to state-of-the-art algorithms.

articleTitle: Multi-UAV Trajectory Planning and Tracking Via Improved Informed-RRT* and MPC Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: For the study on the multi-UAV cooperative execution of complex tasks, this paper divides multi-UAV cooperative tasks planning into three parts: task allocation, path planning and trajectory tracking. Firstly, the specified task is assigned for each UAV by choosing Hungarian algorithm as the task allocation algorithm. Secondly, an improved Informed-RRT* algorithm is employed to plan the trajectory of the multi-UAV system. Then, a trajectory tracking controller is designed by using a model predictive control method. Finally, the simulation results are carried out to verify the effectiveness of the designed method.

articleTitle: A Classification Algorithm for Breast Masses Based on the Combination of Bidirectional ConvLSTM Network and Coordinate Attention Module
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: To address the problem of breast mass size difference, in order to make the model pay better attention to breast mass information, this paper proposes a benign and malignant classification algorithm for breast masses based on the combination of bidirectional ConvLSTM network and coordinate attention mechanism, so as to meet the medical clinical needs. Firstly, the mass region obtained through multi-view mass detection is cropped as the input of the two-branch classification network, and the feature information of the mass region in different views on the same side is extracted separately; secondly, the SE sub-module of the MBConv module in the EfficientNet network is replaced by the coordinate attention module to enhance the expressive ability of the network to learn small masses; then, the bidirectional ConvLSTM module as the feature fusion module to connect the correlation between the two views, which then realizes the benign and malignant mass diagnosis. After experimental validation on the DDSM public dataset, it is concluded that the method proposed in this paper can obtain the values of accuracy and AUC of 0.910 and 0.963, respectively, which can effectively improve the benign and malignant mass classification accuracy.

articleTitle: The Research on Cloud Monitoring System Architecture of Flight Test
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: To meet the needs for real-time monitoring of future test flights, this article introduces the current monitoring system status and development trends, and proposes a flight test cloud monitoring system architecture, and elaborates the key technologies for implementing flight test cloud monitoring systems in detail. The system-related technology should be used for reference in the test flight.

articleTitle: Crash Severity Prediction Based on Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Vehicle-vehicle crash occur frequently and is one of the major causes of casualties. In order to reduce the severity of accidents, this article conducts a severity prediction study on crash data in Texas, USA, from 2017 to 2019. Based on the permutation feature importance (PFI), this article divides the crash influencing factors into five aspects and ranks them by weight. Then, the one-dimensional crash data is converted into a two-dimensional grayscale image according to certain rules. Then, the convolutional neural network (CNN) is used to extract and enhance important crash features in the image. By adjusting the network structure and related parameters, multiple iterative trainings are performed to obtain an effective prediction model. Compared with other methods, the method in this paper can enhance the generalization ability of the model and improve the prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Buoy Autonomous Depth Determination Control Algorithm Based on Improved Whale Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In order to realize the reliable control of autonomous depth setting in the course of buoy movement, an autonomous depth setting control algorithm based on Improved Whale Optimization Algorithm (IWOA) is proposed in this paper, utilizing the improved whale optimization algorithm to realize the self-tuning of PID control parameters. To improve the convergence speed and accuracy of control parameter self-tuning, in the initialization stage of the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA), a Logistic mapping is introduced to generate the initial population, enhancing diversity among the initial solutions. During the iterative optimization process, an adaptive inertia weight and a non-linear convergence factor are employed to balance the global and local search phases. Additionally, a Lévy flight strategy is incorporated to prevent the algorithm from getting stuck in local optima, thereby improving its accuracy. PID parameters of buoy depth determination system of IWOA and WOA were optimized in MATLAB/Simulink respectively. The results show that IWOA optimized PID control has smaller overshoot and stability time, faster iteration speed and better optimization results than WOA optimized PID control.

articleTitle: Feasibility Analysis of State-of-the-Art Time Series Models for Wind Power Forecasting with Irregular Missing Data
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Data missing is prevalent in wind power generation data due to equipment failures and maintenance. However, the current mainstream wind power forecasting models all discuss performance in the absence of missing data. To address this problem, this paper aims to investigate the feasibility of popular time series forecasting models for wind power prediction task with irregular missing data. In the experiment, the performance of the Timesnet, Dlinear, MICN and PatchTST is analyzed through a large number of experiments. In general, these four models can work in absence of missing data. Specially, the MICN model performs the best, while the TimesNet model exhibits the highest robustness to data missing. Besides, after reaching optimal performance, the effectiveness of the algorithms gradually deteriorates as the data missing rate increases.

articleTitle: Implementation of an Unmanned Gas Inspection System for Coal Mines
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In response to the current situation of coal mine gas inspection and the shortcomings of traditional manual gas inspection and intelligent gas inspection, this paper introduces an implementation method of an unmanned coal mine gas inspection system. On the basis of constructing the lora wireless network in the coal mine underground, this method realizes a network communication method of local wireless network and underground backbone ring network; Considering that gas inspection sites in coal mines involve many communication and power supply cables that are difficult to lay, wireless multi-parameter inspection equipment, electronic fence equipment, etc. have been adopted to achieve automatic inspection and alarm; Finally, in conjunction with the upper computer system software and mobile APP application, the fully automatic control process of gas inspection was completed, ensuring the authenticity and reliability of gas inspection data, greatly saving human resources investment on the coal mine site.

articleTitle: Fast Algorithm for VVC Video Image Coding Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: VVC (Versatile Video Coding) encoding has achieved outstanding results in terms of encoding performance, with a bitrate saving of around 50% compared to previous versions at the same image quality. However, it is complicated and time-consuming, which makes it difficult to be popularized. In this paper, we propose a convolutional neural network for the most time-consuming block segmentation stage, which directly predicts the optimal segmentation of the CU blocks of images in a video sequence during the coding process. After the training of tens of thousands of CUs, the final prediction accuracy can be up to 90% while maintaining the quality of the final video.

articleTitle: Flexible Actuator Based on Dielectric Elastomer and Conductive PAM Hydrogel Electrodes
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In recent years, dielectric elastomers have been widely used as electronic functional materials in the field of flexible electronic devices, such as flexible actuators, flexible sensors, and flexible energy storage devices. This paper designed and constructed four types of centimeter level flexible actuators with different dielectric elastomer layer thicknesses based on Ecoflex dielectric elastomer material and conductive polyacrylamide (PAM) hydrogel material, and conducted high-voltage excitation response experiments on them. When the thickness of the dielectric elastomer layer was 0.5 mm, the flexible actuator achieved the maximum area strain of 27% and 26.5% under the action of the triangular wave voltage signal (max 10 kV) and step voltage signal (10 kV), respectively. The research content of this paper provides an effective approach and technical solution for the design and construction of flexible actuation components, and promotes the development of flexible drive technology.

articleTitle: A Noval Event-IMU Odometry Based on Quadtree-Accelerated Asynchronous Event Corner and Graph Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Event cameras, a type of neuromorphic vision sensor, capture pixel-level intensity changes to generate asynchronous event streams with precise timestamps. They offered several advantages, including a high dynamic range, high temporal resolution (low latency), and freedom from motion blur. Leveraging event information and corresponding visual algorithms holded significant promise for the development of robotic autonomous systems. In this paper, we proposed an event-inertial odometry method based on asynchronous event corner detection and tracking. We introduced a novel approach for fast event corner detection using a quadtree-based method, ensuring a spatiotemporally uniform distribution of corners. Additionally, we presented a high-precision state estimation framework that combines IMU measurements and event corner observations through graph optimization. To assess the performance of our method, we conducted experiments using a publicly available dataset and compared our results with state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. Our findings demonstrated that our approach excels in terms of both accuracy and speed.

articleTitle: A Fully Digital Implementation of A Reward-Modulated STDP Synapse
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Reward - modulated Spike - Timing - Dependent Plasticity (R-STDP) is a learning technique for Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) that adjusts the synaptic plasticity induced by Spike-Timing-Dependent Plasticity (STDP) using an external learning signal. This paper presents a fully digital architecture of R-STDP, and proposes, for the first time, a circuit design for the generation and modulation of the external learning signal reward. The design was validated on a Field-Programmable Gate Array(FPGA), demonstrating a power consumption of 0.205W at a frequency of 250MHz. The experimental results were consistent with the software simulation. The circuit achieves excellent tradeoffs among performance, resources, and latency. The hardware-friendly implementation of R-STDP holds the potential to facilitate SNNs on-chip learning, as well as enable applications in fields such as robotics and automatic control.

articleTitle: Assessment of Perturbability in Module Parameters of Image Classification Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: While various modules and structures have emerged to enhance the accuracy in the development of neural networks, research into their stability remains limited. When constructing networks for specific tasks, modules that balance accuracy and stability play a crucial role in mitigating attacks stemming from perturbation of weight parameters. The entire model can also be accurately encrypted through the knowledge of the known modules and structures within the model. The stability of modules and structures in neural networks in the field of image classification was explored in this paper. On the CIFAR-10 and Mini-ImageNet data sets, Lenet-5, GoogLeNet, ResNet, and ResNeXt models were chosen to examine the impact of different module and quantity on model's accuracy through weight parameters perturbations. It was found that convolution, Batch Normalization (BN), residual, group convolution each exhibited unique variation patterns on both data sets when subjected to perturbations. Furthermore, the accuracy could be effectively preserved by the shortcut connections during disturbances. In addition, modules which improve accuracy also could reduce stability. This study contributes to understand the stability and disturbance characteristics of different modules and architectures in the field of image classification.

articleTitle: Adaptive Generalized Super-Twisting Sliding Mode Control for PMSM Servo System
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Aiming at improving the anti-disturbance capability and response speed of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) system, a novel adaptive gains generalized super- twisting controller (AGSTC) is constructed for speed loop. By introducing adaptive control gains into the generalized super- twisting algorithm (GSTA), the proposed AGSTC eliminates the requirement to determine the upper bound of disturbance. The proposed AGSTC improves the dynamic performance of the PMSM system. Experiments are carried out to present the effectiveness of the proposed AGSTC.

articleTitle: Dynamics Knowledge Graph-Based Digital Thread for Machine Tool Dynamics Digital Twin
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Machine tool dynamic digital twin has the property of being multidimensional and multiscale, subject to the working position and processing speed. Thus, the data-driven twin models exhibit both discreteness and finiteness. It requires a method to fuse various twin models to build a complete digital twin. However, the digital thread-driven digital twin lacks efficient information fusion methods to provide it with evaluation and prediction capabilities. Therefore, the paper proposed the dynamic knowledge graph (DKG)-based digital thread for constructing a complete dynamic digital twin. Dynamic knowledge graph -based digital thread guides the construction of multidimensional and multiscale twin models, and enable information fusion for twin models. At the same time, the knowledge fusion capability based on machine learning provides the knowledge extension for the complete dynamic digital twin (DGT), so that the dynamic digital twin has the ability of prediction and evaluation. It is the first time that we propose the digital thread construction method based on dynamic knowledge graph. This approach has shown excellent predictive performance in dynamic digital twin of the machining process at the machining center. The analysis results show the effectiveness and performance of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Data-Based Collaborative Control for Air Supply System of PEMFCs
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The air supply system in Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFCs) is a multi-input multi-output (MIMO) system with inherent disturbances, which presents complex nonlinearities and strong coupling. Traditional mechanistic modeling approaches are inadequate for this system. This paper aims to leverage a purely data-based modeling technique and proposes a coupled control architecture to effectively manage and optimize the air supply system. The MIMO model-free adaptive controller (MF AC) achieves its control obj ectives by simultaneously controlling the air compressor speed and throttle valve opening, ensuring that the air mass flow rate and cathode pressure of the air supply system track the desired values. By comparing the single-input single-output compact form dynamic linearization MFAC (SISO CFDL-MFAC) with the MIMO CFDL-MFAC, we propose that the latter exhibits better control performance for the air supply system of PEMFCs. This is because the MIMO CFDL-MFAC can handle multiple input and output variables simultaneously, taking into account the system's coupling effects, capturing the system's complex dynamic characteristics more effectively, and controlling it in a more precise manner.

articleTitle: A Numerical Method for the Compliance Analysis of Continuum Robots
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Continuum robots are characterized by their high compliance and dexterity. However, these features also lead to a reduction in accuracy. While many literature on continuum robots address aspects such as design, kinematics, and statics, there are few in-depth studies on the compliance of these robots. This paper introduces a numerical approach for obtaining the compliance of continuum robots, taking into account the influences of cable tensions, external loads, and gravity. Based on this method, an analysis to examine the compliance of a two-section cable-driven continuum robot within its workspace under various load conditions is conducted. Results indicate that the robot's compliance is correlated with the external load and the shape of the robot. Moreover, the compliance of the robot in the x direction and y direction is highly related with the distance between the robot's tip end and axes. These conclusions could be useful for the active compliance control of the robot.

articleTitle: Research on Robots Path Planning Based on Recurrent Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: At present, the latest application of innovative robotics has led to an increasing utilization of autonomous robots in industrial processes. Existing path planning almost concentrate on single robot and ignore the planning for multiple robotics. Additionally, almost planning methods through deploying an optimization algorithm and not concern the implementation of learning models. In this work, we devise a novel recurrent neural network for multiple E-puck robots and achieve the self-moving in the simulation environment. Additionally, the recurrent network can identify the collision situation and avoid it. Furthermore, we compare our model with existing path planning methods to estimate the performance of our model. From our simulation results, we can observe that our model can achieve the planning for multiple robots with reasonable amount of collision occurrence times and computation costs.

articleTitle: A Trajectory Prediction Method for Drifting Buoy Based on GA-DNN Model
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The floating movement of the buoy is a complex movement under the action of the Marine environment background field. In this paper, a deep neural network model (GA-DNN) optimized by a genetic algorithm is constructed based on the environmental factors affecting buoy drift, such as surface current and profile current, and the trajectory prediction of buoy drift is realized. Through a series of experiments, the GA-DNN model constructed in this paper has better prediction performance than the traditional deep neural network and linear regression model. The three evaluation indexes of RMSE, MAE, and R2 and distance and angle errors are improved, and the effective prediction of buoy trajectory is realized.

articleTitle: Prediction of Output Pressure of Dredge Centrifugal Pumps Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Dredge centrifugal pumps are extremely important equipment for CSD and TSHD in the field of dredging. It is mainly used to extract, transport and lift granular matter, so as to realize dredging and reclamation works. During the actual operation of the dredge centrifugal pump, its operation performance directly affects the efficiency of the dredgers. Relying on the operating process parameters of the CSD pump of medium-coarse sand blowing and filling project, this paper established a machine learning output pressure prediction model. By predicting the pressure output performance of different pump speed, conveying flow and conveying concentration, the operating performance of the dredge centrifugal pump is accurately obtained. The results show that the established model can accurately predict the output pressure of CSD pump of medium-coarse sand blowing and filling project, which provides an important theoretical basis for the optimization of the CSD dredging process with different conveying distances.

articleTitle: Research of Hybrid Collaborative Filtering Algorithm in Course Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: At present, as people's awareness of learning increases, more and more learning resources appear on the Internet, and online courses are becoming more and more popular. Recommendation research for online courses can help users get the quality courses they need faster. This article integrates the optimized Apriori algorithm and the user-based collaborative filtering algorithm and recommends more appropriate courses to users based on this hybrid model. The results are more reasonable than those obtained by relying on any of the above algorithms alone.

articleTitle: A Continuous Hand Movement Recognition Method for sEMG Signals Based on BiLSTM Network and Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Surface electromyographic(sEMG) signals are considered to be the most suitable physiological feedback signal for acquiring human movement intention. Human-computer interaction technology based on sEMG signals is widely used in intelligent prosthesis control, sign language recognition, skeletal rehabilitation and other fields. Aiming at the problems of poor model stability and low precision in continuous hand motion recognition based on sEMG signals, a new deep learning method (BiLSTM-Att) based on LSTM and multi attention mechanism was proposed. Firstly, the RMS features of sEMG signals of different channels were extracted, and then the mapping model between motion and sEMG signals was constructed, and combined with the time-space information of signals, the historical information of depth features was mined. Finally, different feature subspaces were input to more stably and accurately predict the metacarpophalangeal joint angle in real time. BiLSTM-Att was evaluated on 6 finger movements of 15 subjects in the NinaPro DB2 dataset and compared with CNN-BiLSTM network, LSTM and TCN in the same operating environment. The experimental results show that the average CC, RMSE and NRMSE (0.85±0.03; 9.29±1.88; 0.10±0.01) was significantly better than that of CNN-BiLSTM(0.81±0.05, p<0.001; 10.12±2.09, p<0.001; 0.11±0.01, p<0.001), LSTM(0.75±0.06, p<0.001; 11.60±2.71, p<0.001; 0.13±0.02, p<0.001) and TCN(0.71±0.06, p<0.001; 12.40±2.60, p<0.001; 0.14±0.02, p<0.001), which indicates that BiLSTM-Att of the paper can estimate finger continuous motion more stably and accurately.

articleTitle: Research on Pipeline Climbing Gait Control of Snake Robot Based on Compound Gait
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: To address the instability issues encountered by snake robots during climbing variable diameter pipes and curved pipes, a compound gait that combines decoupled climbing gait and serpentine gait is proposed. By utilizing sensor data to assess the climbing environment, and combining with extended Kalman filtering (EKF) for control parameter estimation, a parameter adaptive control method is designed. This method can improve the accuracy of perception environment and enhance the motion stability performance. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed adaptive climbing gait is validated through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Scoring and Classification Multi-Functional Pose Matching Network Combining Alignment and Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In recent years, posture matching has found extensive applications in rehabilitation training. However, the recent known study has primarily concentrated on posture scoring performance while neglecting the incorporation of classification capabilities. To address this limitation, this paper introduces a novel concept and presents a functional module that integrates both classification and scoring, with the objective of generating similarity and classification outcomes simultaneously. This study chose three yoga poses from Kaggle as the original dataset, and then used OpenPose to extract the skeletal features of the joints and other parts of the images, and used the Scale Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT) algorithm to align the images as the input dataset. This study designed an attention-based Siamese network combined with a classification module. Additionally, this study combined the SENet attention module with the VGG-16 backbone. Two images are input and pass through 13 convolutional layers, 5 max pooling layers, 1 dropout layer and two fully connected layers, and then combine with CosineEmbeddingLoss and CrossEntropyLoss functions to obtain their posture classification and similarity. Through the training and testing of the model, excellent experimental results can be obtained. The outcomes of posture extraction and alignment exhibit remarkable clarity. The output results indicate a similarity of 0.941 for identical postures, -0.390 for different postures, an accuracy rate of 0.997, and a loss value of 0.112. These findings offer precise posture classification and scoring results for patients.

articleTitle: A High-Precision SLAM System Based on Lidar, IMU and Wheel Encoders
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In autonomous driving map generation, vehicle localization plays a crucial role. To address the limitations of single sensor positioning in terms of accuracy and robustness, this paper proposed a multi-sensor fusion SLAM algorithm based on lidar. The algorithm integrated information from lidar, IMU, and wheel encoders. Building upon the FAST-LIO2 framework, this paper first integrated IMU data to obtain an initial pose estimation. Then, the system's velocity was observed and corrected by using the velocity values from the wheel encoders. Subsequently, the distorted lidar point cloud was undistorted using this pose estimation. Finally, the lidar point cloud was matched with the map, and a second pose correction was performed based on point-to-plane residual observations. Using this refined pose estimation, the lidar point cloud was projected onto the world coordinate system, completed the mapping of the surrounding environment. Experimental evaluations were conducted on both dataset and real-world environments, and the results demonstrated that incorporating the wheel encoder velocity as a direct observation of the system's velocity benefited the SLAM algorithm in improving localization accuracy.

articleTitle: FA-YOLO: An Improved YOLOv5 Sonar Image Target Detection Model Based on Focal Attention
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Sonar image target detection plays a critical role in underwater applications such as sunken ship detection and underwater vehicle tracking. Distortions in sonar imaging often result in varying representations of the same target in different positions. Furthermore, the presence of underwater environmental noise and interference from other moving objects often leads to challenges in low contrast and poor separability between targets and backgrounds in sonar images, making accurate underwater target detection challenging. To address these issues, this paper proposes a sonar image object detection model named FA-YOLO, based on an improved YOLOv5 architecture using Focal Attention. The FA-YOLO model leverages the Focal Net to enhance discriminative features between targets and backgrounds, emphasizing target-weighted information while suppressing background features during the feature extraction process. Subsequently, it employs a convolutional block attention module to adaptively focus on and enhance target-specific channel and spatial feature information, thereby significantly improving the model's target detection accuracy. Experimental evaluations conducted on two sonar image target datasets, UATD, demonstrate that the proposed model achieves an mAP@0.5 of 98.1%, outperforming comparative models. Furthermore, experimental validation on the small sample dataset SCTD yielded an mAP@0.5 of 98.9%, confirming the model's generalizability and adaptability to small sample datasets. The results illustrate the promising application prospects of FA-YOLO in underwater target detection.

articleTitle: A Decimal Scaling Normalization Encoder-Decoder Deep Network for Modeling in the Nonlinear Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Deep learning predictive networks are extensively employed for modeling and predicting nonlinear systems due to their superior nonlinear modeling capabilities. They are able to capture the hidden characteristics given the presence of noisy and complex nonlinearities in data collected by sensors, and provide satisfactory performance such as modeling accuracy. In this paper, we have proposed the so-called Decimal Scaling Normalization Encoder-Decoder Deep Network (DSED) to deal with the modeling problem for certain complex nonlinear systems. Our approach relies on a codec structure, and the data undergoes decimal scaling normalization, significantly enhancing modeling accuracy. Experiments involving the modeling of tank vibration reaction forces have been conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, and the results confirm the model's strong modeling capability.

articleTitle: Interpretable Fault Diagnosis for Industrial Processes Based on Multi-Task Meta-Feature Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Traditional machine learning methods often present themselves as black-box models, unable to provide interpretability for the decision-making process, which is unacceptable in industrial processes. To overcome this issue, this work proposes an interpretable fault diagnosis method based on multi-task meta-feature learning (MT-MFL). By simultaneously learning fault meta-features and fault class differences, the model can generate more expressive and interpretable feature representations. Additionally, the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method are demonstrated through validation experiments conducted on a three water tanks model. The experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms traditional machine learning methods significantly in terms of fault diagnosis performance and result interpretability.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Methods for Ship Classification: From Visible to Infrared Images
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Deep learning methods have achieved excellent performances on visual tasks of target recognition and classification. The rapid development of autonomous seafaring vessels comes up with the requirement to recognize other maritime ships day and night. However, the recognition of ships based on the deep neural networks may not always access the results as expectation when the ships are under the nighttime environment. To this issue, we consider the ship recognition task under the deep learning framework with paired visible images and infrared images. In this article, we propose an end-to-end convolutional network based on visible images and infrared images of the autonomous seafaring vessels. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our model, we choose the V AIS dataset to test the performance of classifying the maritime ships. Experimental results show that the proposed network outperforms the state-of-the-art methods based on the V AIS database.

articleTitle: A Multi-Layer Fusion Method for Infrared and Visible Images
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The fusion of infrared and visible images serves as a pivotal technology to overcome the limited information-capturing capability of sensors in extreme environment. To address the various practical challenges, choosing an appropriate fusion strategy can be a prerequisite to ensure the performance of a fusion model. In this paper, a novel infrared and visible image fusion strategy is developed based on a multi-layer fusion framework. First, the image is decomposed into multiple parts based on the low-rank decomposition theory. Second, a fusion strategy tailored to the unique feature of each modality is employed. Then a multi-layer feature fusion strategy is proposed to enhance the fusion performance. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed strategy is demonstrated in an experiment based on the TNO dataset, where the desired fusion result is achieved with marked enhancement in the visual quality.

articleTitle: Research on Defect Recognition Method of Digital Pipeline Negatives Based on Improved YOLO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Pipe welding is widely used in industry. Defects such as cracking, porosity, slagging, imperfect shape, under-welding and cracking may negatively affect the strength and sealing performance of the welded structure, and the evaluation of weld defects is time-consuming and labor-intensive, so intelligent recognition of weld defects has become crucial. In this paper, the characteristics and morphology of various defects such as weld cracks, porosity, slag entrapment, imperfect shapes, and crazing are studied in detail, and algorithm optimization and model training are carried out for these characteristics. In addition, different types of welding defects commonly found on negatives were considered, including volumetric and planar defects, slag entrapment, and under-welding. Through an in-depth study of the imaging characteristics and basic properties of these defects, we have developed a comprehensive target detection system designed to automatically identify and categorize common weld defects on negatives, providing an efficient and accurate tool for pipeline weld quality control. Ultimately, this research aims to provide a complete solution for pipeline welding quality control by combining advanced computer vision and deep learning techniques, such as improved YOLO algorithm, to improve the efficiency of defect detection and identification, thereby providing the industry with a more reliable and efficient means of digitally evaluating pipeline negatives.

articleTitle: Research on Mobile Robot Path Planning Based on A* Algorithm with Specific Node Priority
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Aiming to address the problem of robots based on QR code navigation being unable to reach QR code nodes in time to correct dead reckoning errors, this paper proposes an improved A* algorithm. The improved method firstly groups all QR code nodes into a dedicated node list, separated from ordinary nodes. It then applies a QR code reward function to weight the nodes in the dedicated node list. Finally, it modifies the weighting of the heuristic function to prioritize generating paths that pass through specific nodes in order to reach the target node. Through simulation experiments, the proposed improved method increases the number of times the robot passes through the QR code nodes while ensuring path safety, effectively reducing dead reckoning errors, and improving the accuracy and efficiency of robot navigation.

articleTitle: Book Recommendation Algorithm Based on Time Information and Book Feature
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The development of online transactions and the explosive growth of book resources have led to increasingly diverse demands and choices for books among users, consequently changing the requirements for book recommendations. Traditional collaborative filtering algorithms are commonly employed in various recommendation systems, including book recommendations, to recommend targets based on nearby users or similar items. However, these algorithms fail to consider that a user's reading habits may change over time and do not account for the influence of popular books on similarity calculations between users and books, thereby interfering with the accuracy of recommendations. To address these issues, an improved cosine similarity calculation method is proposed in this study. This method reduces the impact of popular books on recommendation results by incorporating a penalty term while also capturing the dynamic changes in users' reading interests through the introduction of a time attenuation function. The effectiveness of this enhanced book recommendation algorithm is validated using the Goodbooks dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that this algorithm achieves lower Mean Absolute Error (MAE) compared to traditional approaches, leading to significantly improved quality in recommendations.

articleTitle: A Short-term Traffic Flow Forecasting Method Based on SVM-PSO-BP Combined Model
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The accuracy of traffic flow forecasting has a significant impact on intelligent traffic control. In recent years, scholars pay more and more attention to traffic flow forecasting based on combined models. Considering the strengths and weaknesses of the nonlinear regression SVM and BP neural network, this paper puts forward a short-term traffic flow forecasting method that use the combination of SVM and BP models. To get better forecasting performance of the BP neural network model, the article uses PSO(Particle Swarm Optimization) algorithm to optimize some parameters of the BP model, finally construct the SVM-PSO-BP combined model. Using RMSE(Root Mean Square Error) and MAE (Mean Absolute Error) as indicators to evaluate the model performance, and traffic flow data collected from British highways as the dataset, the models are respectively trained and used for prediction on weekdays and weekends. Through experiments, it is found that the proposed SVM-PSO-BP outperforms a single prediction model in both evaluation indicators, and can better reflect the changes and trends of traffic flow.

articleTitle: Research on Trajectory Planning of Orchard Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In contrast to typical scenarios, orchards present a more intricate environment characterized by numerous irregular obstructions. This complexity often leads to the generation of zigzag paths when employing conventional path planning algorithms. Moreover, the challenge is compounded by the orchard's slippery terrain and the fact that traditional path planning approaches do not consider robot kinematics, necessitating abrupt changes in acceleration. Such conditions make it arduous for orchard robots to follow these paths effectively. To mitigate these issues, this study introduces the minimum Jerk principle, which focuses on minimizing the rate of change in robot acceleration, as the cost function for optimizing the paths devised by standard path planning methods. The paper culminates in an empirical evaluation using a robot in an orchard setting. Experimental results demonstrate a substantial reduction in the robot's angular velocity fluctuations and a 12% decrease in tracking time, compared to paths generated by conventional methods.

articleTitle: Predefined Performance Tracking Control Design for a VTOL Aircraft System
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This work discusses the predefined performance tracking control issue of a vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) aircraft system. By using the designed control performance function, the constrained error signal of the aircraft system can be switched into an equivalent unconstrained signal. Moreover, fuzzy logic systems are introduced to cope with the aircraft system's unknown nonlinear dynamics. And then, adaptive fuzzy sliding control laws are designed by combining the fuzzy control method with the sliding mode control technique. Based on the designed control law, it is not only ensured that the outputs of the VTOL aircraft system can track the desired trajectories, but also that the tracking errors are constrained within a predefined range. Finally, the availability of proposed control method is testified through simulation example.

articleTitle: Non-Destructive Identification of Grape Species Based on Near-Infrared Spectroscopy and TLNET Network
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In recent years, precise identification of food products has become a crucial aspect in establishing market value, meeting consumer demands, and facilitating effective brand management within the food industry. Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) technology, a nondestructive testing method, provides a new approach for detecting food adulteration without causing damage. Advanced machine learning techniques are integrated for intelligent and accurate identification of adulteration. This article introduces TLNET, a deep learning network that utilizes NIR technology for precise grape variety classification. The proposed model combines the advantages of Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) architectures to capture both spatial and sequential dependencies within spectral data. Additionally, an elastic net mechanism is implemented to improve classification accuracy and reduce overfitting risks. To investigate the effectiveness and stability of the model, a comparative analysis was conducted between three conventional machine learning algorithms, namely K-N earest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest (RF), and Support Vector Machine (SVM), and five deep learning models, including Visual Geometry Group (VGG), Gated Recurrent Unit(GRU), Residual Network (Res Net), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM),Re-current Neural Network (RNN), and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). The TLNET network achieved impressive accuracy of 100% in classifying grape varieties, as evidenced by the results. This approach not only offers a pioneering and effective method for non-invasive identification of grape varieties, but also presents potential for identifying other agricultural products.

articleTitle: Topic Mining of Alzheimer's Disease Field Based on BERTopic
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease is the most common progressive neurodegenerative disease in clinical practice, and it is also one of the main causes of disability and death in the elderly. Alzheimer's disease has become a major brain disease that seriously endangers the health of the elderly and affects the sustainable development of society and economy. As the number of people with Alzheimer's disease (AD) rises, the research on AD continues to heat up. Exploring the topic of literature research on Alzheimer's disease is intended to better sort out the research in this field. In this paper, the topic modeling method of BERTopic was applied to the literature on Alzheimer's disease research from 2000 to 2019, to identify the main research directions in this field, and to analyze the changing trend of topic intensity. Twenty research topics in this area were finally identified, and research on amyloid beta and tau was found to have declined significantly since 2016. In addition, this paper also evaluated and compared the quality of topic extraction of two models, LDA and BERTopic, and verified that the accuracy and effectiveness of topic mining results of Alzheimer's disease research based on BERTopic were superior to those generated by LDA model.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Validation of Typical Human Machine Interaction Tasks Based on GOMS Modified Model
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: On the basis of improving the basic model through experiments in the early stage and obtaining a modified GOMS model, in order to verify its effectiveness, this article adopts an experimental method based on typical human-machine interaction tasks in complex information systems, combining Analytic Hierarchy Process with GOMS model analysis. Based on task analysis, typical human-machine interaction task experiments are carried out, Verify the task analysis of the model by comparing human task execution time with the task execution time predicted by GOMS task analysis theory through experiments. The experimental data results show that the error between GOMS predicted time and actual time is between 0.31% -14.02%, which is relatively close and can be used for human-machine interaction task analysis, usability design and evaluation of information systems.

articleTitle: Non-Singular Terminal Sliding Mode Control Based on Finite-Time Extended State Observer for Robotic Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: During the control process of robotic system, problems such as slow speed and low accuracy in trajectory tracking control caused by external disturbance and internal parameter uncertainties always happen. Aiming at the above problems, an improved finite-time extend state observer (FTESO) based non-singular fast terminal sliding mode control (NFTSMC) with funnel boundary constraints is proposed in this paper. Firstly, a FTESO with special feedback mechanism, is designed to estimate both the unmeasured states and lumped uncertainties. In addition, by incorporating the error transformation into the sliding mode surface, a novel finite time controller is designed to improve the anti-interference ability and dynamic performance. In order to confirm the superiority of the suggested control strategy, varies comparison simulations are conducted at the end.

articleTitle: Trajectory Tracking Method for Wheel-Leg Climbing Robot on Complex Facade
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Maintenance operations on large metal facades, such as petrochemical storage tanks and civilian ships, are crucial for ensuring their safe operation. Traditional manual methods are plagued by poor safety, low operational efficiency, and significant resource wastage. Thus, this study investigates the motion mechanics and trajectory tracking control methods for maintenance robot systems on metal facades, resulting in the development of a high-performance and adaptive wheeled-legged magnetic adhesion climbing robot prototype. Utilizing the principles of virtual kinematics and degrees of freedom theory, the study extracts multidimensional constraints and independent coordinate variables to establish a coupled disturbance kinematic model for the robot. To address pose errors caused by uncertainties in body parameters and external disturbances during operations, an adaptive extended observer and sliding mode torque controller are proposed, introducing an adaptive extended observer sliding mode control method for trajectory tracking. Lyapunov theory is employed to demonstrate the stability and convergence of the designed controllers. Through simulation experiments, the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed trajectory tracking control method are substantiated.

articleTitle: Design and Obstacle Crossing Research of Wheeled-Leg Hybrid Unmanned Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This article proposes a obstacle-crossing control strategy for a quadruped wheeled-leg unmanned robot, achieving the ability to climb vertical walls while considering ground contact. Initially, this control strategy considers the motion states of the legs in the wheeled-leg robot. By detecting whether the legs are lifted or in contact with the ground, the controller parameters of the wheeled-leg robot are adjusted, allowing for torque control of each joint actuator. Subsequently, the robot's motion is controlled by planning leg end trajectories and body velocity to complete the obstacle-crossing process on vertical walls. Finally, the proposed motion control method and foot trajectory strategy are implemented through Simulink. Controller parameters are adjusted within Simulink, and the simulation is conducted to achieve obstacle-crossing on vertical walls for the wheeled-leg robot. This control method and trajectory planning enable the wheeled-leg robot to overcome vertical wall obstacles, significantly enhancing its passability and environmental adaptability.

articleTitle: A Tensegrity Robotic Fish Driven by a Sliding Crank-Pendulum Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This paper develops a tensegrity robotic fish, composed of the tensegrity structure and sliding crank-pendulum mechanism.
