The fish body is made of tensegrity structures and the sliding crank-pendulum mechanism transforms rotation of the motion into the swing of a pendulum rod. By connecting the two parts with joints and elastic cables, the robotic fish can realize flexible swing motion by changing the balance of internal forces of the tensegrity structure using the motor. The driving torque of the motor is analyzed by simulating the connection parameters between the pendulum rod and the fish body. Then a prototype is designed and fabricated. Experimental results present that with the increase of stiffness, the speed-frequency curve gradually presents an approximate linear growth, and higher stiffness means better swimming performance at a higher driving frequency zone.

articleTitle: HiGOD: Hierarchical Multi-granularity Object Detection based on Prior Label Knowledge Structure for Open World Perception
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Existing object detection methods are mostly under the closed-world assumption and often inadequate in dealing with the complexity and unpredictability of real-world scenarios. Transitioning from closed-world settings to open-world settings has emerged as a pivotal research direction in visual perception. While existing object detection methods excel at identifying objects at the finest granularity, they often overlook the hierarchical relationships between different object categories and the coarse-grained recognition results. However, this prior knowledge hierarchical structure, which remains stable regardless of environmental changes, holds potential as a valuable resource to assist in open-world perception. In this paper, we propose a hierarchical and multi-granularity object detection method built upon prior label knowledge structures. We construct a tree-like knowledge structure to organize labels in a hierarchical manner. By introducing a hierarchical matched loss during training, our approach enables the network to produce hierarchical output and achieve better performance. Additionally, we present a decision fusion module to achieve flexible hierarchical output that is data-adaptive. Our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in detecting previously unseen targets in open-world scenarios, even in the presence of lower-quality input samples, and exhibit superior robustness and transfer ability compared to traditional object detection algorithms.

articleTitle: ROS2-based locator optimized autonomous navigation robot
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With the rapid development of robot technology, mobile robots are gradually becoming mature and are widely used in warehousing, logistics and environmental detection. However, the navigation robot working indoors has a great impact on its positioning and navigation accuracy due to the strong activity of family members and the high dynamics of the working environment, and the operation effect is not satisfactory. At the same time, the traditional ROS system cannot be well adapted to the future working environment due to poor stability and poor correlation of multiple robots. Based on the latest ROS2 system, this paper designs an autonomous navigation robot, and optimizes the front-end parameters and back-end parameters of Cartographer that make the established map more complete. By optimizing locators and planners in navigation2 that makes the robot more effective use of the environmental space and efficiently carries out indoor path planning and navigation.

articleTitle: Robotic Precision Force Control in Optical Machining a Fuzzy Admittance Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This paper presents the development and implementation of a Fuzzy Variable Admittance Control (FVAC) system for precision optical machining with collaborative robots. Incorporating fuzzy logic into the admittance control framework, the system adapts to real-time machining dynamics, maintaining force control with high accuracy. Experimental results on a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$40 \text{mm} \mathrm{x} 40\text{mm}$</tex> quartz glass demonstrated the system's capacity to keep force tracking error within 0.3N, reducing the surface form error from PV 472.8nm to 178.3nm and RMS from 93.1nm to 29.8nm. This method outperforms traditional fixed-parameter admittance control, promising enhanced efficiency and precision in optical manufacturing processes.

articleTitle: CPG Motion Controller Based on Van der Pol Nonlinear Oscillator for a Quadruped Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of mobile robot technology, its application in power inspection has become increasingly prevalent. Among these applications, legged robots have garnered significant attention due to their exceptional environmental adaptability. This paper focuses on studying the motion controller for quadruped robots. Firstly, a Central Pattern Generator (CPG) based on Van der Pol nonlinear oscillator is proposed. Secondly, a motion controller based on the above CPG is designed for the walk gait and the trot gait of the quadruped robot. The controller can achieve stable gait control by modifying the coupling topology coefficients and the coupling phase differences. Finally, Simulink-Adams joint simulation is employed to validate the effectiveness of the above motion controllers.

articleTitle: Optimization Method of Roadside Unit Location for Information Propagation
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This study proposes an optimization model for roadside unit location to reduce multi-hop communication time in road networks. Since the location cost will affect the quality of the location strategy, and thus the multi-hop communication time of the road network, consider increasing the penetration rate of connected vehicles on the road section to reduce the road network communication time. Model this problem as a nonlinear mixed integer programming. The model is solved using piecewise linear algorithm. The roadside unit location strategy is generated under the condition of unifying the traffic flow of each road section. On this basis, the roadside unit deployment strategy is improved by adjusting the vehicle density of certain road sections. The results show that the location strategy proposed in this study meets the same delay requirements while reducing the deployment cost.

articleTitle: The Detection Method of Rice Seedling Tray Hole Seeding Quantity Based on Improved YOLOv5s
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Detecting the number of seeds in rice seedling tray holes is crucial for ensuring the seeding efficiency of pneumatic precision seeders and adjusting working parameters. To address issues such as low accuracy and poor real-time performance in seedling tray hole seeding quantity detection, this study proposes an improved YOLOv5s-Seed model based on the YOLOv5s architecture. The small target detection performance of rice grains is improved by high-resolution feature mapping redirection connection. Additionally, Coordinate Attention is incorporated into the neck network to better focus the model on essential feature information of rice grains for feature fusion. Furthermore, SPD-Conv building blocks are introduced in the backbone and neck networks to minimize the loss of fine-grained information. The rice grain can be detected by the YOLOv5s-Seed model. Finally, the hole seeding quantity of the seedling tray is obtained by calculating the number of intersections of the prediction boxes. The experimental results show that the precision (P), recall (R), and mean average precision (mAP) of the improved YOLOv5s-Seed are 2.7, 5.0, and 3.5 percentage points higher than those of the original model, respectively, and each image takes 0.025 s. The improved model lays the foundation for seedling tray hole seeding quantity detection in precision seeders, providing technical support for precision agriculture and intelligent seeding.

Author Keywords: rice seedling tray hole seeding quantity detection

articleTitle: Research on Semantic Segmentation Model of Codec Lightweight Road Image Based on Deep Separation and Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With the rapid development of automatic driving technology, semantic segmentation of road image has become a hot research object of semantic segmentation. In order to better solve the problems of long image prediction time and rough category edges in road image segmentation, this paper proposes a segmentation network model based on deep separation and attention mechanism based on the optimization design of the backbone network of DeepLabV3+model. By improving the adaptability of the BNeck structure composed of DSC backbone network, reducing the number of model parameters to improve the prediction speed of the model, through the combination of spatial attention mechanism and channel attention mechanism, the weight of the model is more distributed among the regions of interest and channels, and finally using the overall architecture of encoder decoder to design a more efficient segmentation model.

articleTitle: A Depth Estimation Network Integrated of Foreground Target Enhanced by Optical Flow and Binocular Vision
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In order to improve the accuracy of motion information detection in the unmanned driving field, this research proposes a deep learning network - OFSMDE, which combines optical flow, masking and binocular estimation. Optical flow is the two-dimensional projection of a three-dimensional moving object on a plane, and depth is the three-dimensional information obtained from the camera state and scene. These tasks emphasize the target through the semantics information to improve the estimation accuracy. OFSMDE consists of optical flow prediction module, mask module and orbit depth analysis module. OFSMDE introduces semantics segmentation to enhance the consistency between depth and optical flow information while feature extraction is carried out, and further accurately distinguishes foreground and foreground information by masking, then fuses features through context network at cost, and finally obtains high-resolution disparity by regression. OFSMDE has achieved good performance on KITTI 2015 data set. Compared with the reference algorithm PSMNet, the 3-pixel error is only 1.83%, and it has excellent performance in low-contrast environment with strong robustness.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Dynamic Modeling Method for External Torque Estimation of Robot Manipulators
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This paper introduces a hybrid modeling approach designed to estimate external forces in robot manipulators, with a focus on achieving high-precision force estimation while minimizing reliance on force/torque sensors. Traditional methods used for robot dynamics modeling and identification often grapple with unmodeled dynamics, system measurement noise, filtering delays, and equipment vibrations, all of which contribute to significant errors in the resulting dynamic models. To address these challenges, this paper leverages neural networks to mitigate the discrepancies in the physical model. The process commences with the application of the Newton-Euler method to perform dynamic modeling of the robot manipulators. Subsequent parameter identification is conducted to establish the physical model governing the robot manipulators' dynamics. Building on this physical model, a backpropagation (BP) neural network is employed to create a data-driven model of the model errors, thereby further enhancing model accuracy. To validate the effectiveness of this approach, external torque estimation experiments were carried out on a six-axis robot manipulators platform utilizing a Beckhoff controller. The experimental results affirm the method's capability to significantly improve the accuracy of external torque estimation in scenarios where force/torque sensors are unavailable.

articleTitle: Road Grid Segmentation in Desert with Geometry and Appearance Features
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Presently, the detection of drivable areas is one of the most important tasks for autonomous driving of UGV (unmanned ground vehicle). In off-road scenes, the accessible areas have complex appearance. There is no obvious boundary between obstacles and roads. Besides, each single frame of Lidar scans is greatly affected by the slope of ground. Therefore, this article proposes a road segmentation method based on LiDAR. Firstly, through multi-frame accumulation and Gaussian filtering, a local ground height map is obtained. Then we extract slope information based on the height map. The current scanned point cloud appearance features and slope features are fused to achieve ground grid segmentation in a bird's eye view. In training, this article uses dense labels obtained from multi-scans to supervise sparse scan scenes. Experiments has shown that the fusion of the two features improved the accuracy of the algorithm. This paper also collected 2500 frames of point cloud in Alax, and created an off-road dataset for the Gobi Desert. On this dataset, our method outperforms several comparison methods and can be implemented in real-time operation.

articleTitle: Autonomous Conscious Humanoid Robot System
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In order to enable intelligent robots to have autonomous consciousness and make decisions autonomously, and generate behaviors safely and ethically, an autonomous conscious humanoid robot (ACHR) architecture is proposed and designed in this paper. The ACHR is mainly composed of mental system, environment perception system and behavior generation system. When the robot is stimulated externally in an environmental interaction, or generates an internal motivation due to an internal need, the stimulation is analyzed and goals of the robot are generated. Then goals are decomposed and logically sorted through the mental system, and sent into the behavioral decision-making system. Finally, behavior decision that meet moral ethics and safety principle is transferred to the behavior generation module so that the robot can generate behaviors. Compared with existing humanoid robots, the ACHR proposed in this paper combines large-scale models with generative intelligence technology and it is more autonomous. The framework of autonomous conscious humanoid robot proposed in this paper can promote the development of conscious robot in the future and provide a new idea for the development of intelligent robots.

articleTitle: DgrCLR: Dual Gradient Reinforcement Contrastive Learning for Coal Gangue Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In the application of coal gangue visual classification, the influence of strong vibration and uneven illumination in an industrial environment causes the fuzzy boundary of the target and reduces the degree of discrimination of sample features. The existing contrastive learning methods cause apparent gradient degradation due to model and design limitations, leading to fuzzy sample classification failure. Getting rid of the samples with poor annotation effects and alleviating gradient degradation are critical issues in improving the accuracy of coal gangue classification. This paper proposes DgrCLR, a dual gradient reinforcement coal gangue classification algorithm based on improved contrastive learning. By designing the Hybrid reinforcement module and Multi-scale feature fusion module, the gradient degradation is alleviated, the dependence on labeled samples is reduced, and the detail representation ability of the model is improved. The experimental results show that the highest accuracy of the DgrCLR model for coal gangue classification is 85.4%, much higher than that of traditional supervised deep learning models. In addition, the gradient strength of DgrCLR is 20 times or higher than that of SimCLR in some model layers by gradient strength summation comparison.

articleTitle: A Game-Theory Based Collision-Avoidance Solution for Two Automated Vehicles in Lane-Reduction Scenario
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Automated Vehicles (AVs) must be able to avoid the collision between two vehicles, like Manual Vehicles (MVs) do, in lane-reduction scenario (a special lane-change case) where two lanes converge and two traffic flows merge, i.e., to resolve the right-of-way (RoW) conflict between two vehicle-users (assume only one user per vehicle). Aimed at programing AVs to resolve the RoW conflict between two AVs in lane-reduction scenario, we do jobs as follows: (i) we affirm that a RoW conflict between two MVs is solved by the implicit game-theoretic negotiation between two users, where the user—whose demand for RoW is weaker-yield RoW to the other user, meeting an user's self-interest (on the priority of RoW) and both users' mutual interest (on collision avoidance); derived from the insight, we clarify that the solution for RoW conflict between two AVs lies in game-theoretic methods following distributed/interactive multi-agent decision-making paradigm; (ii) we propose an explicit negotiation model (i.e., 2-player non-zero-sum game model) of the priority of RoW to formalize the interaction/interdependence between two AVs' decision-makings (i.e., choices of velocity-adjusting action for AV-users' self/mutual-interests); (iii) we design/prescribe a kind of joint-payoff of the game, which quantifies two AV-users' demands for RoW, thus leads to the Nash-equilibrium(ria) solution(s); (iv) we compute the Nash-equilibrium(ria) of the game, i.e., the optimal (anti-coordinative) velocity-adjusting joint-action(s) where the AV-user—whose demand for RoW is weaker—yield Row to the other AV-user, to resolve the RoW conflict and avoid any collision, i.e., realize the joint maximization of each AV-user's self-interest and both AV-users' mutual interest.

articleTitle: Robotic Demonstration Learning Stability-Accuracy Trade-Off: From an Energy Function Learning Viewpoint
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Learning a globally asymptotically stable (GAS) autonomous dynamic system (ADS) is one of the most popular approaches for the robotic demonstration learning. However, the GAS guarantee will inevitably scarify the demonstration learning accuracy. In this paper, we try to ease the stability-accuracy contradiction by focusing on ensuring the ADS's local stability instead of its global stability. Specifically, an energy function with locally unique-minimum property, called NS-QLF, is designed and learned on the demonstration set to serve as a local stability certificate of the ADS. Then, a locally stable ADS with a predefined region of attraction (RoA) is learned based on the NS-QLF and sequentially optimization techniques. Both simulation and experiments are conducted to validate that the learned ADS can accurately transfer human-like skills to the robot.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Method of NARX and DS-Attention Applied for the State of Health Estimation of Lithium-ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Due to the presence of capacity regeneration and random disturbances during the degradation process of lithium-ion batteries, the capacity decay curve of lithium-ion batteries exhibits a non-linear and unstable trend. Therefore, accurately estimating the SOH of lithium-ion batteries is critical to ensuring the safety and reliability of electrical device. This paper presents a hybrid method of nonlinear auto-regressive model with exogenous inputs neural network (NARX) and DS-Attention. The NARX model improves estimation performance by incorporating exogenous inputs as auxiliary factors, while the DS-Attention model is utilized to establish the mapping relationship between the input and output. The DS-attention model proposed in this paper is a specialized method of recurrent neural network (RNN), which improves the attention mechanism by adding division and self-adaptive functions. The division function improves the performance of NARX by effectively distinguishing external inputs and outputs. In addition, the self-adaptive function optimizes the query features in the attention mechanism. Experimental results demonstrate the exceptional performance of the proposed algorithm compared with similar algorithms by using different training set sizes and different numbers of neurons, and the advantage of DS-Attention is more obvious in the case of a smaller sample set.

Author Keywords: Nonlinear auto-regressive models with exogenous inputs neural network

articleTitle: Distributed Optimal Scheduling of Integrated Energy Systems Based on Federated Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This paper addresses the economic optimization scheduling problem of integrated energy systems while taking the data privacy concerns into account. While traditional optimization methods can address scheduling problems in specific scenarios, they often struggle to adapt rapidly to the stochastic variations in loads and renewable energy sources. Data-driven deep reinforcement learning offers significant advantages in tackling this issue, but it involves handling a substantial amount of sensitive data. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a method that combines collaborative learning among multiple intelligent agents with privacy-preserving techniques to maximize system efficiency and protect user privacy. Initially, each intelligent agent undergoes local training, followed by the uploading of model parameters to a global server for privacy protection and federated averaging. Global average parameters are then distributed to individual agents for local model updates, with this process iterated multiple times until satisfactory performance is achieved. Experimental results demonstrate that this method achieves secure transmission and processing of user data through privacy protection measures, while achieving significant success in low-carbon economic dispatch. With the support of differential privacy mechanisms, the integrated energy system achieves an excellent balance between privacy protection and solution performance.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Object Tracking with Vision-Language Adaptive Fusion and Alignment
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The current CLIP-based multi-modal deep learning has been widely used for various tasks and has achieved leading results. Traditional vision-language multi-modal tracking paradigms extract vision and language features separately and then fuse them, which is difficult to train end-to-end. This paper proposed a framework for synchronous feature extraction and fusion of vision and language. Specifically, adaptive multi-modal attention operations are performed on language-template and language-search region respectively. Then a vision module performs self-attention and cross-attention between template and search region, integrating the long and short-term clues of the target to model the position of the target in the search region. Finally, model learns a unified feature representation through the modality alignment module. By contrastive learning, this method can extract and fuse vision-language features efficiently. Extensive experiments are conducted on three benchmark tests, TNL2K, OTB99-Lang and LaSOT. Compared with other state-of-the-art methods, this method achieved promising results and outperformed state-of-the-art on TNL2K and OTB99-Lang. Finally, this paper conducted plenty of ablation experiments to demonstrate the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Steel Strips Surface Defect Detection Algorithm Combining Balance Mechanism and Dynamic Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In response to the suboptimal detection efficiency and reduced accuracy of conventional defect detection algorithms applied to steel surface inspection, this research introduces a novel approach based on improved Faster R-CNN for detecting defects on the surfaces of steel strips. Firstly, deformable convolution layers have been introduced into the backbone network to enhance its modeling capability. Secondly, the Balanced Feature Pyramid (BFP) from the Libra Region Convolutional Neural Networks (Libra R-CNN) is incorporated to facilitate the integration of features across various levels, thus reinforcing the original feature representation. Lastly, a combination of the IoU-balanced Sampling mechanism and the Dynamic Label Assignment (DLA) mechanism is employed to ameliorate defect detection accuracy. Experimental evaluations conducted on the NEU-DET dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed defect detection approach, resulting in a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 78.0%. Notably, this performance surpasses the baseline Faster R-CNN model by 2.9%, signifying a substantial improvement in detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Surface Defect Detection of Medium and Thick Plates Based on Yolov8 Network
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Steel is one of the important basic industrial raw materials, and the development of steel production technology directly affects the infrastructure construction, the development of manufacturing industry and the prosperity of the national economy. The identification of surface defects on steel plates has garnered increasing attention. Such defects not only impede the ability of medium and heavy plates to meet user production specifications but also pose the risk of significant production accidents. These challenges can have an immeasurable adverse impact on the production enterprise. Due to the swift advancements in computer vision, vision-based steel plate surface inspection technology has reached a high level of maturity. We collected images of steel plate surface defects, this encompasses the detection of various defects such as overburning, pits, compressed rust skin, and other irregularities originating from the production line of a domestic medium and heavy steel plate factory, and used five models (yolov8, yolov5, Faster-RCNN, RCNN, and DETR) for training and detection after pre-processing techniques such as labelling and data enhancement. Upon evaluating the detection outcomes, it becomes evident that the Yolov8 model exhibits robust accuracy and rapid computational speed when applied to the task of detecting defects on steel surfaces. This proficiency lends dependable technical support for various applications, including industrial quality inspection and the analysis of surface defects. Furthermore, the performance of Yolov8 under different sets of loss functions are evaluated, and the optimal setting is selected for surface defect detection.

articleTitle: Lightweight Semantic Segmentation for Workshop Environments Incorporating Attention Mechanisms and Multiscale Features
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In the context of work environments like factory workshops, addressing the multi-scale challenge posed by the presence of semantic targets is essential, along with resolving the real-time constraints inherent in workshop production. We propose the proposition of enhancing the MobileNet network as backbone and subsequently constructing the position and channel attention mechanisms, along with the fusion of multi-scale features, to formulate a lightweight semantic segmentation network model (PCMuti-Net). The network model employs an encoder-decoder architecture to enhance spatial information retrieval. Within the encoder, we augment MobileNet by incorporating the channel attention mechanism, thereby modifying the network layer structure to diminish computational costs and enhance real-time performance. In the decoder, the position and channel attention mechanisms are integrated, alongside the design of a depthwise separable atrous pyramid pooling model and a fusion module of deep and shallow features. This configuration is designed to extract multi-scale contextual information effectively. Through the selection of classical lightweight models and subsequent comparative experiments conducted on both a public dataset and a self-constructed factory dataset, PCMuti-Net demonstrates notable performance. It achieves up to 92.5% Mean Pixel Accuracy (MPA) and 76.6% Mean Intersection over Union (MIoU) for workshop scene targets. Furthermore, it operates at 38.98 billion floating-point operations per second (GFLOPs) with an inference speed of 53.29 frames per second (fps). The semantic segmentation accuracy and real-time capabilities surpass those of the comparative experimental models, showcasing PCMuti-Net's ability to effectively balance accuracy and real-time performance.

articleTitle: Application of LSTM Networks in the Temporal Analysis and Prediction of Earth Pressure Balance Shield Parameter
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Amid the rising trend of intelligent and unmanned shield tunneling construction, an industrial smart application has been developed to predict crucial parameters of shield boring by integrating Earth Pressure Balance (EPB) shield tunneling scenarios with artificial intelligence. Real operational data from EPB shield activities has been meticulously detected to eliminate abnormal data during the tunneling process. Employing both the Pearson Correlation Coefficient (PCC) and Gray Relation Analysis (GRA), pertinent features have been effectively extracted by assessing the relationship between shield parameters and the speed of the screw conveyor. A Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network model has been meticulously trained and optimized to facilitate the self-adjustment of the screw conveyor speed within EPB shields. Drawing on the current shield parameters, the model is proficient at delivering precise real-time predictions for screw conveyor speed adjustments. The self-adjustment model for the screw conveyor speed in EPB shields is deployed in the field, completing real-world testing experiments. Subsequent to its deployment, the model has demonstrated exceptional accuracy, precision, very low computational latency, and commendable robustness, thereby presenting practical engineering significance.

articleTitle: Study on Ultra-Short-Term Prediction of Solar Irradiance Based on Multi-Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Addressing the challenge of ultra-short-term solar irradiance prediction, a method based on multi-feature fusion is proposed. This approach takes into account the influence of various meteorological parameters and cloud-related factors, extracting cloud category and cloud amount features from all-sky images. Subsequently, these cloud categories and cloud amount features are integrated with meteorological features to realize the fusion of environmental numerical features and image features, thereby enhancing the computational parameters for solar irradiance prediction. Furthermore, we have enhanced the design of the MLP-Mixer network for solar irradiance prediction, effectively reducing prediction errors. Comparative experiments with other models demonstrate superior predictive performance of the network model.

articleTitle: Insider Threats Risk Warning and Traceability Based on User Behavior Entity Analysis and Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This paper proposes a method to detect and trace insider threats in tobacco industry databases. The method is based on user entity behavior analysis and knowledge graph. It tackles the challenges of insider threat detection, such as high detection costs and tracing difficulties. The proposed method extracts salient features and augments attack vectors to improve classification performance. Additionally, it encodes user behavior as high-quality color images, overcoming the limitations of conventional grayscale encoding. By analyzing the UEBA and KG detection results, the threat cause can be traced. The proposed method demonstrates its effectiveness and superiority on a benchmark dataset.

articleTitle: Aggregation Mechanisms in Federated Learning for Enhancing Robotic Visual Obstacle Avoidance
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In the realms of robotics and the autonomous driving field, deep learning has been a game-changer for applications such as perception, obstacle avoidance, SLAM, etc. The success of these deep learning algorithms, however, relies on large-scale data sets for training, raising substantial privacy concerns for users unwilling to share raw data. Addressing this issue, our study explores federated learning in robotics to leverage its inherent privacy-protection attributes. Federated learning, a privacy-conscious method within the machine learning paradigm, has become increasingly prominent in recent years. More importantly, an essential aspect of our work is the assessment of diverse aggregation mechanisms within the federated learning framework, aiming at enhancing robotic functionality. We gather data and implement a federated learning model using various aggregation algorithms in visual obstacle avoidance contexts. The results demonstrate considerable variances in the performance of these algorithms, indicating that certain federated learning aggregation methods can exceed the performance of traditional centralized learning models. This study affirms the feasibility and advantages of federated learning in robotic applications, publicly available on github.
